```{r setup, include = FALSE}

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)

# the data objects are built by data-raw/processing-scripts/process-hatchery-data.R and saved in data/
data_files <- list.files(here::here("data"), pattern = "^KFNFH_", full.names = TRUE)
walk(data_files, load, envir = globalenv())

final_objects <- c(
  "KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "KFNFH_pond_growout", "KFNFH_LRS_ESS_adult_collection",
  "KFNFH_hatchery_release", "KFNFH_pen_survival", "KFNFH_adfluvial_early_rearing",
  "KFNFH_LRS_ESS_incubation_hatch", "KFNFH_age_facility_lookup", "KFNFH_mortality_events",
  "KFNFH_mortality_events_summary", "KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly", "KFNFH_capacity",
  "KFNFH_broodstock_spawned")
stopifnot(all(map_lgl(final_objects, exists)))

pct <- function(x) suppressWarnings(parse_number(x))

# every data frame is printed as an HTML table that wraps its text and fits the page (first 25 rows); glimpse() lines fit the page too
options(width = 100)
knit_print.data.frame <- function(x, ...) {
  n <- nrow(x)
  knitr::asis_output(knitr::kable(head(x, 25), format = "html", digits = 3, table.attr = 'class="fit"',
                                  caption = if (n > 25) sprintf("first 25 of %s rows", format(n, big.mark = ","))))
}
registerS3method("knit_print", "data.frame", knit_print.data.frame, envir = asNamespace("knitr"))
```

# Purpose

The hatchery data objects of the package are **built in `data-raw/processing-scripts/process-hatchery-data.R`** and saved to `data/`.
This document does not build anything: it loads the saved objects and explores them (a `glimpse()` and summaries of each), runs QC checks and plots
on each one, describes each object, and holds a draft data dictionary.

**Where values come from.** Every value is taken from the annual reports (PDF text and tables) or the hatchery Excel workbooks. The mortality events are
written in the script from the report text, and each event gives the report and page it comes from (`citation`).

**How the objects are built.** `process-hatchery-data.R` has these sections:

| Part of the script | What it does |
|---|---|
| PARSE PDF FILES, PROCESS TABLES | Report tables of each year (FY2021-FY2025, cached in `data-raw/pdf-tables/`) into per-year objects; intermediate objects `hatchery_release_2021_2024`, `adult_collection_2023_2024`, `pond_growout_reports_2021_2024`, `pen_survival_reports_2024` |
| 2. INPUTS FROM THE EXCEL WORKBOOKS AND THE REPORTS | Reads the workbooks and report text/tables: mortality spreadsheets, production harvest, spawning crosses, broodstock, the age/facility lookup, collections and releases, capacity, and the mortality events (description, phrase in the report, loss and severity tier). |
| 3. FINAL OBJECTS | Merges the FY2021-2024 tables with FY2025 and the workbook inputs and saves the objects: lookup, collection and release history, pond grow-out, incubation and hatch, adult collection, hatchery release, net pens, early rearing, mortality events (E01-E37), monthly pond mortality, capacity, broodstock spawned. |

# Assumptions and decisions

Every number in the objects comes from the annual reports or the hatchery workbooks. The items below are the places where a rule, a reading of the text, or a
choice between sources decides a value. They were made while building the objects, and each one should be confirmed or changed.

| Area | What was assumed or decided |
|---|---|
| Mortality events E01-E28: descriptions | Each event is written from the FY2021-2024 report text, checked against the report pages named in `citation`. Wording keeps the report's hedges ("suspected", "likely", "may have") and leaves out details the report does not give (for example a pond's location when the report does not say where). The `category` is a label chosen from the report's description: events whose cause the report does not state or that the report does not call a disease are labelled `other` (E05, E09, E10, E14, E15, E16). `mortality_event` is no when the report describes no fish deaths (E07, E13, E18, E20, E21, E26, E27, E28). |
| Mortality events: losses typed from the text | E03 and E04 are 100% ("all perished", "total losses within days of hatch"). E26 and E27 are 0%: the report says no sucker mortality was observed (it also gives 96% harvest survival for the Gerber pens), so 0% means no observed mortality. **No `percent_lost` (tier "Qualitative only") where the report gives no loss that belongs to the event:** E07 (2,175 of 2,479 fish harvested; the report does not say what happened to the rest), E11 ("an estimated 200+ fish lost" of 1,999 stocked; the number at risk is not clear), E14 (86% is survival of the whole RZB treatment, not the event) and E16 (752 fish died in the event; 19.7% is survival of the whole tank). E22 has none either ("several thousand fish"). Percentages computed from reported counts (E01, E08, E12, E17, E19, E23) and from reported survival (E25, 100 minus 45%) are arithmetic on reported numbers; E18's 54.8% is an apparent loss because the report presumes the missing fish escaped. |
| Mortality events: severity tier | Over 70% is Catastrophic, 30-70% Major, 10-30% Moderate, under 10% Minor; an event that is not a mortality event is "Near-miss" if its loss is 0 and "Non-mortality" otherwise; an event with no percent is "Qualitative only". These thresholds are a choice (they are not in the reports). |
| Mortality events: fish lost (`n_mortality`) | Filled for E01, E11 (200, the report's minimum), E12 and E16 (752) among E01-E28 (where the reports give the fish lost); counts that could be computed for others (for example E08, E17, E19) are left `NA`. For E29-E37 it is filled whenever a count exists. |
| FY2025 events E29-E37 | The category, `mortality_event` and `confidence` labels and the wording of the description columns are mine, written from the FY2025 report. **E29:** the loss is the fish at the start minus (harvested + harvest-day deaths), the definition of the `Survival` column of `Sheet1`, and `Sheet1` is used rather than the Production Harvest workbook (they disagree on the harvested fish). **E33:** "just under 70% survival" is taken to be the P10 cycle in the Production Harvest workbook (sheet Spring 2025). **E34:** the event window runs from the first July day with 10 or more dead fish to the last day the staff note stratification; the loss is recorded deaths only, over the fish at the start in the Production Harvest workbook (sheet Fall 2025). **E35:** uses the Table 8 total of 3,562 deaths, not the 3,652 in the report text. **E30, E32, E37:** no number of fish at risk is given, so there is no percent. |
| Pond grow-out | A completed cycle listed in two reports is kept once (the later report's row, 44 cycles); a cycle reported in progress is replaced by its completed record; `fiscal_year` is the year of the report that lists the cycle; numeric pond IDs ("0") become "P0"; `weight_gain_lb` merges a misspelled duplicate column; `life_history` is "ESS" when the lot name contains "ESS"; the FY2025 report tables are read by column position, with months and growth split from one text cell. |
| Age lookup | All built by rules: net pens age = operation year minus capture year; ponds age class = fiscal year minus the lot's collection year (4 means 4 or older), East Side Springs and mixed lots "other", wild or salvage lots "wild"; a cycle counts in the fiscal year it was stocked and in the fiscal year it was harvested; `starting_count` is the fish at the start of the first cycle harvested in the year. |
| Capacity | The pond counts and sizes are typed from report sentences, and each sentence is checked against the report text. FY2024 is set to 22 ponds because the four A-series ponds were demolished early in the year. The FY2022 report says "nearly 2.1 acres" but its own pond counts give 2.38 acres, and 2.38 is used. The planned row's year (2028) is an assumption: the FY2025 report only says the build-out is "beyond 2027/2028". Indoor gallons are summed from the tank lists by text pattern, counting each research rack sump (4 x 180 gallons) as capacity. |
| Rounding | `total_eggs` is rounded to whole numbers, `hatch_percent` to one decimal (and captive `eggs_per_mL` to two), as in Excel, so FY2025 incubation values differ slightly from the raw workbook values (for example 3,255.78 is 3,256). |
| Incubation and adult collection | FY2024 `family_groups` is the number of males listed (the table has no such value). Short PIT tags (4-5 characters) are expanded to the full tag when exactly one tag in the FY2025 workbook or report table ends with them. Adult `sex` M/F is recoded to Male/Female. |
| Collection and release history | `larvae_collected` is taken from Table 7 (30,150 for FY2024) rather than Table 1 (30,142); `total_released` is the sum of the four release columns; `broodstock_on_station` is the number parsed from "approximately" or "over" in the report text; FY2021 `new_broodstock_reported` (300) is read from "300 broodstock selected". |
| Early rearing | `restock` is set from the word "Restock" in the culture-unit name; `date` is the first date when a row lists two days. |
| QC checks | The tolerances (for example 5% for eggs, 2 points for survival) and the plausible ranges (for example fork length 300-1000 mm) were chosen for this document. |

# Inputs used for the checks

The FY2025 Production Harvest workbook is read here for two cross-checks (pond grow-out, and the September 2025 harvest). One row per pond cycle,
sheets `FALL 2024`, `Spring 2025` and `Fall 2025`:

```{r production-harvest-workbook}
ph_path <- here::here("data-raw/hatchery-resources/FY2025 Supporting Excel Tables/FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx")

extract_col <- function(raw, pattern) {
  matched <- names(raw)[str_detect(str_squish(names(raw)), regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))]
  if (length(matched) == 0) return(rep(NA_character_, nrow(raw)))
  if (length(matched) == 1) return(raw[[matched]])
  exec(coalesce, !!!as.list(raw[matched]))
}
excel_date <- function(x) as.Date(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)), origin = "1899-12-30")

production_harvest_fy2025 <- map2(c("FALL 2024", "Spring 2025", "Fall 2025"), c("Fall 2024", "Spring 2025", "Fall 2025"), \(sheet, season) {
  raw <- readxl::read_excel(ph_path, sheet = sheet, col_types = "text")
  tibble(pond = extract_col(raw, "^Pond$"),
         stocked_date = excel_date(extract_col(raw, "^Stocked? Date$")),
         start_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^Start #$"))),
         harvest_date = excel_date(extract_col(raw, "^Harvest Date$")),
         end_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^End # Live$|^End #$"))),
         survival_percent = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(extract_col(raw, "^Survival$")))) |>
    filter(!is.na(pond), pond != "Pond") |>
    mutate(season = season, pond = str_to_upper(pond),
           # some seasons record survival as a fraction (0-1)
           survival_percent = if (!all(is.na(survival_percent)) && max(survival_percent, na.rm = TRUE) <= 1) survival_percent * 100 else survival_percent)
}) |> list_rbind()
```

# Age / facility lookup

`KFNFH_age_facility_lookup` maps each pond or net pen to the age class(es) of the fish held there, by fiscal year. It is the single source of
fish age: `KFNFH_pond_growout` and `KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly` take `age_class` and `starting_count` from it. `age_class` holds classes such as
`"1/2"` or `"wild"`, not a single age.

```{r lookup}
glimpse(KFNFH_age_facility_lookup, width = 100)

KFNFH_age_facility_lookup |> count(fiscal_year)
```

### How the lookup is built

The lookup is built from the workbooks and reports only:

* **Net pens** (UKL and Gerber): `nphistory.xlsx`. Age is the operation year minus the capture year; `starting_count`
  is the number of fish stocked.
* **Ponds** (A, B, C and P series): every pond cycle in the Production Harvest workbooks and the annual report tables.
  A cycle counts in the fiscal year it was stocked and in the fiscal year it was harvested. The age class is that fiscal
  year minus the lot's collection year (4 means 4 or older); East Side Springs and mixed lots are `other`, wild and salvage
  lots are `wild`. `starting_count` is the number of fish at the start of the first cycle harvested in the year.

Facility-years that no cycle or net pen record covers have no row (for example the FY2020 ponds).

# Collection and release history

`KFNFH_historical_collection_release` is built from Table 1 and Table 7 of the FY2025 report, which repeat the full history (FY2016-2025) with updated
numbers; the broodstock columns come from the report text.

```{r historical}
glimpse(KFNFH_historical_collection_release, width = 100)
```

FY2024 `larvae_collected` is **30,142** in FY2025 Table 1, but **30,150** in the FY2024 report (Tables 1 and 4, and the narrative), in FY2025 Table 7 of the
FY2025 report itself, and in the hatchery's own workbook (the cumulative "Total Collected To Date" in `2024 Larval Collection and Early Rearing Summary Data.xlsx`
ends at 30,150). Three sources agree on 30,150, so **the object uses the Table 7 value (30,150) for all years** (it equals Table 1 in every other year). The same workbooks also confirm FY2023 (6,036) and FY2025 (70,049).

# Pond grow-out

`KFNFH_pond_growout` combines the pond tables of the FY2021-FY2025 reports. The Production Harvest Data Sheet workbooks describe the same pond cycles;
for FY2021-2024 their rows match the report rows on pond and harvest date (start numbers are identical; end numbers and survival agree for about 95% of
rows), so they are not appended as a second copy. The script:

1. keeps the report tables as the primary source (they have the full set of columns, including weights);
2. adds FY2025 from the FY2025 report pond tables (Tables 10-12) so FY2025 has the same columns as earlier years;
3. validates the FY2025 rows against the workbook, and would append (flagged `source = "production_harvest_workbook"`) any workbook row that is not in the report tables
   (there are none);
4. replaces a cycle reported as still in progress (no harvest date) in an earlier report with the later, completed record of the same pond and stocking date;
5. removes a completed cycle that is listed in two consecutive reports (44 cycles: 24 in both FY2023 Table 7 and FY2024 Table 6, and 20 in both the
   FY2022 tables and FY2023 Table 5), keeping the later report's row;
6. takes `age_class` and `starting_count` from the lookup.

```{r pond}
glimpse(KFNFH_pond_growout, width = 100)

KFNFH_pond_growout |> count(fiscal_year, source)
```

Validation of the completed FY2025 cycles against the Production Harvest workbook:

```{r pond-validate}
key <- function(d, stock, pond = "pond") ifelse(is.na(d[[stock]]), NA, paste(d[[pond]], d[[stock]]))

pond_2025_report <- KFNFH_pond_growout |> filter(fiscal_year == 2025, source == "annual_report_table")

fy25_check <- pond_2025_report |>
  filter(!is.na(harvest_date)) |>
  mutate(k = key(pick(everything()), "pond_stock_date")) |>
  inner_join(production_harvest_fy2025 |> filter(!is.na(harvest_date)) |>
               mutate(k = key(pick(everything()), "stocked_date")) |>
               select(k, wb_start = start_number, wb_end = end_number, wb_survival = survival_percent),
             by = "k")

tibble(completed_report_rows_fy25 = sum(!is.na(pond_2025_report$harvest_date)),
       matched_to_workbook = nrow(fy25_check),
       start_number_equal = mean(fy25_check$start_number == fy25_check$wb_start, na.rm = TRUE),
       end_number_equal = mean(fy25_check$end_number == fy25_check$wb_end, na.rm = TRUE),
       end_number_minus_morts_equal = mean(fy25_check$end_number - fy25_check$harvest_mortality_number == fy25_check$wb_end, na.rm = TRUE),
       survival_within_0.5 = mean(abs(fy25_check$survival_percent - fy25_check$wb_survival) < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE))
```

For the completed FY2025 cycles, start numbers are identical and survival agrees. The FY2025 report's `End #` counts fish before harvest mortalities, while the
workbook's `End #` is the live count, so `end_number - harvest_mortality_number` equals the workbook value for every matched row.

Ponds with no age class are ponds that are missing from the lookup:

```{r pond-age-gaps}
KFNFH_pond_growout |>
  filter(is.na(age_class)) |>
  count(fiscal_year, pond) |>
  arrange(fiscal_year, pond)
```

(the ESS metadata workbook, identical to report Table 3), with the family-group count and, for FY2025, the second fry count.

```{r incubation}
glimpse(KFNFH_LRS_ESS_incubation_hatch, width = 100)

KFNFH_LRS_ESS_incubation_hatch |> count(fiscal_year)
```

# Adult collection and hatchery release, FY2025

The FY2025 report gives FY2025 versions of both tables, which are added to the FY2023-2024 data.

```{r adults}
glimpse(KFNFH_LRS_ESS_adult_collection, width = 100)

KFNFH_LRS_ESS_adult_collection |> count(fiscal_year, sex)
```

```{r release}
glimpse(KFNFH_hatchery_release, width = 100)

KFNFH_hatchery_release |> group_by(fiscal_year) |> summarise(rows = n(), fish = sum(number_fish, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The FY2025 report states 26,454 fish distributed or transferred ("All Spp." overall total) and `FY25 Fish Distribution.xlsx` has the same table.

# Net pen survival

FY2025 Tables 13 and 14 repeat the full net pen history (identical to `nphistory.xlsx`). The new information is that no production fish were available in
later years, which is recorded as explicit rows with a `note` so these are not mistaken for missing data.

```{r pens}
glimpse(KFNFH_pen_survival, width = 100)

KFNFH_pen_survival |> filter(!is.na(note))
```

# Early rearing

`KFNFH_adfluvial_early_rearing` (the `_2024` suffix is dropped) holds larval culture-unit stocking, mortality and survival for FY2023 (Table 3), FY2024 (Table 5)
and FY2025 (Table 8). The FY2021 and FY2022 reports do not contain an equivalent table.

```{r early-rearing}
glimpse(KFNFH_adfluvial_early_rearing, width = 100)

KFNFH_adfluvial_early_rearing |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(), collected = sum(collected),
            collected_excl_restock = sum(collected[!restock]),
            stocked = sum(stocked),
            survival = round(100 * stocked / collected, 1))
```

`restock` flags rows whose culture unit is a "Restock" (larvae moved back into a tank that was already
stocked). In FY2024 the five restock rows add up to 7,327 fish, which is exactly the difference between the
sum of the `collected` column (37,477) and the 30,150 larvae actually collected; so **sum `collected` only
over non-restock rows (or use `KFNFH_historical_collection_release$larvae_collected`) for collection totals**.
In FY2025 the rows sum to the reported 70,049, which is also the cumulative collected total in the hatchery
workbook, so those restock rows are fish collected that day, not re-counts.

`date_raw` keeps the date text as reported because FY2025 (and some FY2023) entries span two days
(`"5/8/2025 & 5/9/2025"`). `date` is the first date.

Totals in the reports for comparison: FY2023 6,036 collected and 3,969 stocked (65.8%); FY2025
70,049 collected and 65,847 stocked (94.0%). The FY2023 rows sum to 6,037 collected (the report's
total row says 6,036), a one-fish difference inside the report.


# Mortality events (from the report narratives)

Events E01-E28 come from the FY2021-2024 report narratives and E29-E37 from the FY2025 report. Each event is written from the report text
(`process-hatchery-data.R`, section 2c) and gives the report and page(s) it is taken from in `citation`; wording keeps the report's hedges and leaves out
anything the report does not say. E29-E37 take their losses from the FY2025 water quality and mortality workbook (daily sheets and `Sheet1`), the Production Harvest workbook and the report text.

* every event is tied to a phrase in the report that describes it, and the phrase must be on a page named in `citation` (the script stops otherwise);
* `percent_lost` and `n_mortality` are computed from the net pen records (`nphistory.xlsx`), the larval rearing workbook and numbers in the report text,
  and are left `NA` when the report gives no loss that belongs to the event (see the assumptions table);
* `severity_tier` is computed from `percent_lost` with a fixed rule (over 70% Catastrophic, 30-70% Major, 10-30% Moderate,
  under 10% Minor; no loss in a non-mortality event is a near-miss; no number is qualitative only).

```{r mortality-events}
glimpse(KFNFH_mortality_events, width = 100)
glimpse(KFNFH_mortality_events_summary, width = 100)

KFNFH_mortality_events |> count(severity_tier)
```

## FY2025 events (E29-E37)

The FY2025 report (`FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf`) describes the summer 2025 mortality spike and other losses that are not in the FY2021-2024
event list. The losses come from `KFNFH_WQ_FY2025_2 (version 1).xlsx`: the daily pond sheets (`OctobertoDecember_WQ`, `JantoMar_WQ`, `AprtoJun_WQ`, `JulytoSept_WQ`),
which have a `Morts` column, a lot column (`CY`) and a `Comments` column, and `Sheet1`, which gives the fish at the start and at harvest of the
ponds harvested early in September 2025. Where the workbooks do not give a loss, the number in the report text or Table 8 is used. As for the earlier
events, each event is tied to a phrase in the report (the chunk stops if a phrase is missing), the severity tier comes from the fixed rule, and an event with no
percent loss is "Qualitative only" even when the report gives a number of fish.
The events are built in `process-hatchery-data.R` (section FINAL OBJECTS, Mortality events); the FY2025 events are the rows E29 to E37:

```{r events-fy2025-table}
KFNFH_mortality_events |>
  filter(event_id >= "E29") |>
  select(event_id, year, period, category, percent_lost, loss_as_reported, severity_tier, loss_source)
```

Notes on how these events were built:

* **E29** is the ESS2025 lot in ponds C1 and C2. Loss is from `Sheet1`: fish at the start minus (harvested + harvest-day deaths), which is the same
  definition as the `Survival` column of that sheet. The daily logs record fewer dead fish than were lost, because fish that could not be retrieved
  are not counted (the comments note them every day).
* **E34** differs from the report. The report calls it a minor event with 11 dead fish on one morning; the daily log for pond C6 shows deaths on
  every day from 3 to 18 July, with the staff logging bottom dissolved oxygen of 0.2-0.6 mg/L. The event is built from the workbook (the Excel file wins),
  and the report phrase is kept as its citation.
* **E35** uses Table 8 (3,562 deaths, 5.1% of 70,049); the report text says 3,652, which is a transposition because 3,562 is both the table total and 5.1%.
* **E30, E32** and **E37** have numbers of dead fish (or none) but no number at risk in the reports or workbooks, so they have no percent and are qualitative.

**Sheet1 and the Production Harvest workbook do not agree** on the ponds harvested early. `Sheet1` (used above) gives fewer harvested fish than the
`Fall 2025` sheet of `FY2025 Production Harvest Data Sheet_20251107.xlsx`:

```{r sheet1-load}
harvest_2025 <- readxl::read_excel(
  here::here("data-raw/hatchery-resources/FY2025 Supporting Excel Tables/KFNFH_WQ_FY2025_2 (version 1).xlsx"),
  sheet = "Sheet1") |>
  set_names(c("pond", "harvest_date", "initial", "harvested", "harvest_morts", "survival")) |>
  filter(!is.na(initial))
```

```{r sheet1-vs-production-harvest}
harvest_2025 |>
  select(pond, harvest_date, initial, harvested_sheet1 = harvested, harvest_morts_sheet1 = harvest_morts, survival_sheet1 = survival) |>
  left_join(production_harvest_fy2025 |>
              filter(season == "Fall 2025") |>
              select(pond, start_number, end_number_production_harvest = end_number, survival_percent_production_harvest = survival_percent),
            by = "pond") |>
  mutate(difference_in_harvested = end_number_production_harvest - harvested_sheet1)
```

The differences (1,670 fish for C1 and 1,080 for C2) are not the harvest-day deaths in `Sheet1`, so they are not explained by that column. `Sheet1` is used
for E29; the other workbook is shown for comparison.

## Sources of the losses

Each event is tied to the phrase of the report that describes it (`report_phrase`, in the report of `report_year`) and to the page(s) in `citation`, and its loss to the
workbook, table or text in `loss_source`. The script stops if a phrase is not on a cited page, so an event cannot be mis-cited. Event E07 (Gerber net pen emergency harvest, 2021) has no
`percent_lost` because the report states no loss, so its tier is "Non-mortality". Events E11, E14 and E16 have no `percent_lost` either: the report gives the fish lost for E11 (an estimated 200+) and E16 (752) but not a share of the fish at risk, and for E14 only the survival of the whole diet treatment. Event E22 (August 2024 dissolved-oxygen crashes in ponds
P12 and P13) has no `percent_lost`: the FY2024 report only says "the acute loss of several thousand fish between both instances, as well as some chronic losses",
and the pond records cannot be turned into a combined loss (P13's May 2024 stocking of 3,012 fish was split before harvest), so its tier is
"Qualitative only (unquantified)".

```{r mortality-sources}
KFNFH_mortality_events |>
  select(event_id, year, category, percent_lost, severity_tier, citation, report_phrase, loss_source)
```

# Monthly pond mortality (from the mortality spreadsheets)

Age and starting count come from the lookup so all objects use the same age
definition. The FY2024 workbook covers 1 January to 22 September 2024 only (the October to December 2023 quarter and
the last week of September 2024 are missing), so FY2024 totals are a partial year. The P-series pond matrices
in the `FALL 2023 MORTALITY` and `SPRING 2024 MORTALITY` sheets of the Production Harvest Data Sheet workbooks
cover November and December 2023 and could fill part of that gap.

```{r mortality-monthly}
glimpse(KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly, width = 100)

KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly |>
  group_by(fiscal_year, record_type) |>
  summarise(months = n_distinct(month, na.rm = TRUE), mortality = sum(mortality, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
```

The counts (month, pond, number dead) come straight from the three mortality workbooks; `age_class` and `starting_count` come from the age lookup.

# Capacity

```{r capacity}
glimpse(KFNFH_capacity, width = 100)

KFNFH_capacity
```

Pond counts and acreage are read from the facility description of each report. Indoor tank gallons are summed from the tank lists in the reports: the FY2022-FY2024
reports list only the greenhouse tanks (the second indoor building is first described in the FY2025 report), so each year has the value its report supports:
10,360 (FY2021), 12,035 (FY2022), 12,755 (FY2023 and FY2024), 16,395 (FY2025). The planned build-out has no gallons in any report (`NA`).

# Broodstock spawned

`KFNFH_broodstock_spawned` is the number of captive broodstock spawned in spring 2025 by capture year, species and sex, from the summary block of the
"All PIT" sheet of `FY25CaptiveBroodSpawning_FINAL.xlsx`. It is identical to FY2025 Table 4:

```{r broodstock}
glimpse(KFNFH_broodstock_spawned, width = 100)

tables_raw_2025 <- readRDS(here::here("data-raw/pdf-tables/kfnfh_2025_tables_raw.Rds"))
brood_2025 <- tables_raw_2025[[5]] |>
  slice(-1) |>
  transmute(capture_year_raw = `Capture`,
            SNS_F = as.numeric(`...2`), SNS_M = as.numeric(`...4`),
            LRS_F = as.numeric(`...5`), LRS_M = as.numeric(`...7`)) |>
  pivot_longer(-capture_year_raw, names_to = c("species", "sex"), names_sep = "_") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = value)

check_b <- brood_2025 |>
  mutate(capture_year_raw = if_else(capture_year_raw == "N/A", "N/A (not recorded)", capture_year_raw)) |>
  inner_join(KFNFH_broodstock_spawned, by = c("species", "capture_year_raw"))
tibble(rows_in_object = nrow(KFNFH_broodstock_spawned), rows_matched_to_pdf = nrow(check_b),
       females_equal = all(check_b$F == check_b$females_spawned, na.rm = TRUE),
       males_equal = all(check_b$M == check_b$males_spawned, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# QC checks and plots

One subsection per data object. Each has a table of checks (`rows_failing` is the number of rows that break the check; `status` is `pass` or
`FLAG`, and every flag has a note saying what it is) followed by plots. A flag is a property of the reports or workbooks that the package reproduces,
or a documented limitation; it is not corrected in the object. Each subsection ends with a table of missing values (`NA`) for every variable of the object. The flags are collected in the QC summary at the end of this section.

```{r qc-setup}
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

qc_all <- tibble()
qc <- function(object, check, failed, note = "") {
  n_fail <- sum(failed, na.rm = TRUE)
  qc_all <<- bind_rows(qc_all, tibble(object = object, check = check, rows_checked = sum(!is.na(failed)),
                                      rows_failing = n_fail, status = if (n_fail == 0) "pass" else "FLAG",
                                      note = if (n_fail == 0) "" else note))
  invisible(failed)
}
# tables are written as HTML tables with wrapped text and fixed column widths (see the style block above), so they fit the page
qc_table <- function(o) {
  x <- qc_all |> filter(object %in% o)
  if (length(o) == 1) {
    x |> select(check, checked = rows_checked, failing = rows_failing, status, note) |>
      knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="qc-table"')
  } else {
    x |> select(object, check, checked = rows_checked, failing = rows_failing, status, note) |>
      knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="qc-flags"')
  }
}

# missing values of every variable of an object, as a compact HTML table
na_summary <- function(x) {
  tibble(variable = names(x),
         type = map_chr(x, \(v) class(v)[1]),
         missing = map_int(x, \(v) sum(is.na(v))),
         pct_missing = round(100 * missing / nrow(x), 1),
         rows = nrow(x)) |>
    knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="na-table"')
}

fy_start <- function(fy) as.Date(paste0(fy - 1, "-10-01"))
fy_end <- function(fy) as.Date(paste0(fy, "-09-30"))
fiscal_year_of <- function(d) year(d) + if_else(month(d) >= 10, 1, 0)
```

## KFNFH_historical_collection_release

```{r qc-historical}
h <- KFNFH_historical_collection_release
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "one row per fiscal year", duplicated(h$fiscal_year))
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "fiscal years 2016-2025 only", !(h$fiscal_year %in% 2016:2025))
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "total_released = sum of the four releases",
   h$total_released != rowSums(h[c("sarp_release", "fingerling_release", "fry_release", "salvage_release")], na.rm = TRUE))
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "larvae_collected > 0", h$larvae_collected <= 0)
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "salvage length is SL or TL, not both", !is.na(h$salvage_sl_mm) & !is.na(h$salvage_tl_mm))
qc("KFNFH_historical_collection_release", "collection method present", is.na(h$primary_collection_method))
qc_table("KFNFH_historical_collection_release")
```

```{r qc-historical-plot, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
  ggplot(aes(factor(fiscal_year), value, fill = name)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Fiscal year", y = "Fish", fill = NULL, title = "Larvae collected and fish released")
```

## KFNFH_hatchery_release

```{r qc-release}
r <- KFNFH_hatchery_release
o <- "KFNFH_hatchery_release"
qc(o, "number_fish > 0", r$number_fish <= 0)
qc(o, "dispo_date inside its fiscal year", r$dispo_date < fy_start(r$fiscal_year) | r$dispo_date > fy_end(r$fiscal_year))
qc(o, "no duplicate events", duplicated(r[c("fiscal_year", "dispo_date", "species", "lot", "dispo_location", "from_ponds", "number_fish")]))
qc(o, "number_per_lb within 5% of number_fish / weight_lb", abs(r$number_per_lb - r$number_fish / r$weight_lb) / r$number_per_lb > 0.05,
   "rows where the report's fish per pound does not match its own number and weight")

release_vs_history <- r |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(distributions = sum(number_fish, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(KFNFH_historical_collection_release |> select(fiscal_year, total_released), by = "fiscal_year") |>
  mutate(difference = distributions - total_released)
qc(o, "yearly total equals total_released of the historical table (within 1%)", abs(release_vs_history$difference) / release_vs_history$total_released >= 0.01,
   "the distribution table and the collection and release table of the same report do not add to the same total (FY2021 and FY2023, see below)")
qc_table(o)
release_vs_history
```

```{r qc-release-plot, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}

  summarise(number_fish = sum(number_fish, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(fiscal_year, species_group)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(fiscal_year), number_fish)) +

  facet_wrap(~species_group) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
```

## KFNFH_pond_growout

```{r qc-pond}
p <- KFNFH_pond_growout
o <- "KFNFH_pond_growout"
has_stock <- !is.na(p$pond_stock_date)
qc(o, "no duplicate cycles (pond, lot, stock date, harvest date)", has_stock & duplicated(p[c("pond", "lot", "pond_stock_date", "harvest_date")]),
   "a cycle listed in two reports that the script did not remove")
qc(o, "harvest after stocking", p$harvest_date < p$pond_stock_date)
qc(o, "days within 3 of harvest_date - pond_stock_date", abs(p$days - as.numeric(p$harvest_date - p$pond_stock_date)) > 3, "FY2022 rows from the OCR'd image tables")
qc(o, "end_number <= start_number", p$end_number > p$start_number, "fish were added to the pond during the cycle (mostly FY2021 Table 3)")
qc(o, "survival_percent within 2 points of end_number / start_number", abs(p$survival_percent - 100 * p$end_number / p$start_number) > 2,
   "the hatchery's survival is not always end/start (negative harvest mortalities, fish moved between ponds); values as reported")
qc(o, "survival_percent between 0 and 110", p$survival_percent < 0 | p$survival_percent > 110, "FY2021 Table 3: more fish at harvest than at stocking")
qc(o, "growth_mm_day within 0.1 of (end_tl_mm - start_tl_mm) / days", abs(p$growth_mm_day - (p$end_tl_mm - p$start_tl_mm) / p$days) > 0.1,
   "FY2023 Table 7 (and 3 FY2024 Table 7 rows): the reported 'mm/day' equals the length change divided by 30, i.e. mm per 30 days")
qc(o, "age_class present", is.na(p$age_class), "ponds missing from the age lookup")
qc(o, "fiscal_year = fiscal year of the harvest date", !is.na(p$harvest_date) & p$fiscal_year != fiscal_year_of(p$harvest_date),
   "fiscal_year is the year of the report that lists the cycle; reports also list cycles harvested just before or after their fiscal year")
qc_table(o)
```

The script removed 44 duplicated cycles (the same completed cycle listed in two consecutive reports) and kept the later report's row; the first check above confirms
none remain. The growth values that are not mm/day, by report table:

```{r qc-pond-detail}
p |>
  filter(!is.na(growth_mm_day), !is.na(days), days > 0) |>
  mutate(calculated = (end_tl_mm - start_tl_mm) / days, calculated_per_30_days = (end_tl_mm - start_tl_mm) / 30) |>
  filter(abs(growth_mm_day - calculated) > 0.1) |>
  summarise(rows = n(), matches_per_30_days = sum(abs(growth_mm_day - calculated_per_30_days) < 0.05), .by = c(fiscal_year, inventory_source))
```

```{r qc-pond-plots, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 8}
  labs(x = "Fiscal year", y = "Survival (%)", title = "Pond cycle survival as reported")

p |>

  geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
```

## KFNFH_mortality_events and KFNFH_mortality_events_summary

```{r qc-events}
ev <- KFNFH_mortality_events
s <- KFNFH_mortality_events_summary
o <- "KFNFH_mortality_events"
tier_rule <- case_when(
  !ev$mortality_event & !is.na(ev$percent_lost) & ev$percent_lost == 0 ~ "Near-miss (no mortality observed)",
  !ev$mortality_event ~ "Non-mortality (escape/collection/reproductive)",
  is.na(ev$percent_lost) ~ "Qualitative only (unquantified)",
  ev$percent_lost > 70 ~ "Catastrophic (>70% loss)",
  ev$percent_lost >= 30 ~ "Major (30-70% loss)",
  ev$percent_lost >= 10 ~ "Moderate (10-30% loss)",
  TRUE ~ "Minor (<10% loss)")
qc(o, "one row per event_id", duplicated(ev$event_id))
qc(o, "percent_lost between 0 and 100", ev$percent_lost < 0 | ev$percent_lost > 100)
qc(o, "severity_tier follows percent_lost", ev$severity_tier != tier_rule)
qc(o, "report_phrase present", is.na(ev$report_phrase))
qc(o, "citation present and names the report of report_year", is.na(ev$citation) | !str_detect(ev$citation, paste0("FY", ev$report_year, " Annual Report")))
qc(o, "loss_source present when percent_lost present", !is.na(ev$percent_lost) & is.na(ev$loss_source))
qc(o, "event year 2019-2025 and not after its report", ev$year < 2019 | ev$year > ev$report_year)
qc(o, "category is one of the six categories", !(ev$category %in% c("disease", "water_quality", "weather", "predation", "equipment", "other")))
o2 <- "KFNFH_mortality_events_summary"
qc(o2, "same events, in the same order, as KFNFH_mortality_events", s$event_id != ev$event_id)
qc(o2, "percent_mortality = percent_lost", abs(coalesce(s$percent_mortality, -1) - coalesce(ev$percent_lost, -1)) > 0.05)
qc(o2, "n_mortality >= 0", s$n_mortality < 0)
qc_table(c(o, o2))
```

```{r qc-events-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
ev |>
  mutate(label = paste(event_id, str_trunc(location, 38)), label = fct_rev(fct_inorder(label))) |>

  labs(x = "Percent lost", y = NULL, colour = NULL, title = "Mortality events: percent lost", subtitle = "events without a number are not plotted") +
```

## Checks across objects

```{r qc-cross}
o <- "across objects"
early_vs_history <- KFNFH_adfluvial_early_rearing |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(collected_all_rows = sum(collected), collected_excl_restock = sum(collected[!restock]), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(KFNFH_historical_collection_release |> select(fiscal_year, larvae_collected), by = "fiscal_year") |>
  mutate(closest_difference = pmin(abs(collected_all_rows - larvae_collected), abs(collected_excl_restock - larvae_collected)))
qc(o, "early rearing collected (all rows, or without restock rows) equals larvae_collected of the historical table (within 1 fish)",
   early_vs_history$closest_difference > 1, "FY2023: the report's table rows add to 6,037 and its total row says 6,036")
coverage <- bind_rows(KFNFH_pond_growout |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_pond_growout", fiscal_year, ok = !is.na(age_class)),
                      KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly", fiscal_year, ok = !is.na(age_class))) |>
  group_by(object, fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(share_with_age_class = mean(ok), .groups = "drop")
qc(o, "age_class present for at least 90% of records in every fiscal year", coverage$share_with_age_class < 0.9)
qc(o, "FY2025 pond cycles are all in the lookup for FY2025", KFNFH_pond_growout$fiscal_year == 2025 & is.na(KFNFH_pond_growout$age_class))
qc(o, "each FY2025 event cites the FY2025 report", ev$event_id >= "E29" & ev$report_year != 2025)
qc_table(o)
early_vs_history
coverage |> pivot_wider(names_from = fiscal_year, values_from = share_with_age_class)
```

# One age definition everywhere

Every object with a pond or facility now takes `age_class` and `starting_count` from the lookup:

```{r age-coverage}
bind_rows(
  KFNFH_pond_growout |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_pond_growout", fiscal_year, matched = !is.na(age_class)),
  KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly |> transmute(object = "KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly", fiscal_year, matched = !is.na(age_class))) |>
  group_by(object, fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(rows = n(), with_age = sum(matched), share = round(with_age / rows, 2), .groups = "drop")
```

The lookup starts in FY2019 and is sparse before FY2021, so FY2021 and FY2022 have the lowest
coverage. Filling those is listed under remaining gaps.

# Draft data dictionary

One row per column of each data object, with its type, a description and the source of its values. The descriptions are the ones in `R/data.R`
(they are parsed from the roxygen blocks, so editing them there updates this table). The source is a PDF title, or a workbook and sheet name; a column
whose source differs from the rest of its object has its own entry. This is a draft: columns that are not described in `R/data.R` show as "TODO", and
the table is also written to `data-raw/hatchery_data_dictionary.csv`.

```{r dictionary}
pdf_2021 <- "20240912_FY2021_KFNFH_Annual_Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2022 <- "20240830_FY2022 KFNFH Annual Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2023 <- "20240801_FY2023 KFNFH Annual Report_Final.pdf"
pdf_2024 <- "20250619_FY2024 KFNFH Annual Report_Final Draft.pdf"
pdf_2025 <- "FY25 KFNFH Annual Report.pdf"

dictionary_objects <- final_objects
get_object <- function(name) get(name)

# descriptions: \item \code{column}: text lines of each roxygen block in R/data.R
parse_data_r <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path)
  starts <- which(str_detect(lines, "^#' @name "))
  map2(starts, c(starts[-1] - 1, length(lines)), function(from, to) {
    block <- lines[from:to]
    items <- block[str_detect(block, "^#'\\s+\\\\item \\\\code\\{")]
    tibble(object = str_trim(str_remove(lines[from], "^#' @name ")),
           column = str_trim(str_match(items, "\\\\code\\{([^}]+)\\}")[, 2]),
           description = items |>
             str_remove("^#'\\s+\\\\item \\\\code\\{[^}]+\\}:?\\s*") |>
             str_replace_all("\\\\code\\{([^}]*)\\}", "`\\1`") |>
             str_replace_all("\\\\%", "%") |>
             str_squish())
  }) |> list_rbind()
}
documented <- parse_data_r(here::here("R/data.R"))

# default source of each object
source_default <- tribble(

  "KFNFH_historical_collection_release", paste0(pdf_2025, ", Table 1"),

data_dictionary <- map(dictionary_objects, function(o) {
  x <- get_object(o)
  tibble(object = o, column = names(x), type = map_chr(x, \(v) class(v)[1]))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(documented, by = c("object", "column")) |>
  left_join(source_default, by = "object") |>
  left_join(source_overrides |> filter(object != "*") |> rename(source_override = source), by = c("object", "column")) |>
  left_join(source_overrides |> filter(object == "*") |> select(column, source_all = source), by = "column") |>
  transmute(object, column, type,
            description = coalesce(description, "TODO: not described in R/data.R"),
            data_source = coalesce(source_override, source_all, source))

write_csv(data_dictionary, here::here("data-raw", "hatchery_data_dictionary.csv"))

# described in R/data.R but not a column of the object, and columns with no description
documented |>
  filter(object %in% dictionary_objects) |>
  anti_join(data_dictionary, by = c("object", "column"))
data_dictionary |> filter(str_detect(description, "^TODO")) |> select(object, column)
```

```{r dictionary-tables, results = "asis"}
for (o in dictionary_objects) {
  cat("\n\n## ", o, "\n\n", sep = "")
  data_dictionary |>
    filter(object == o) |>
    select(column, type, description, data_source) |>
    knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = 'class="dict"') |>
    print()
}
```

| FY2022 pond tables 3-4 | Embedded as images and OCR'd earlier; `inventory_source` is `NA` for those rows | Re-check against the source images |
| FY2021 pond PIT tag study (Tables 5-7) and FY2022 historical PIT detections (Table 6) | Different table types, never imported | Decide if the model needs them |
| Weight gain and feed conversion | FY2025 start and end weights are now in `KFNFH_pond_growout` (from the report tables), but weight gain is not reported for FY2025 (left `NA`), and feed conversion is not extracted for any year | Compute weight gain from the start and end weights if needed; extract feed conversion from the workbooks (not in the repository) |
| Mortality events E29-E37 (FY2025) | Added from the FY2025 report, the WQ workbook and `Sheet1`. E30, E32 and E37 have no number at risk, and `Sheet1` and the Production Harvest workbook disagree on the C1/C2 harvest | Ask USFWS which harvest count is right and for the number of fish in the tanks after the September harvest |
| Mortality spreadsheets FY2024 Oct-Dec 2023 | Quarter not found | Ask USFWS |
| Age lookup: FY2020 ponds (A1, A2, P5, P11-P15), unoperated FY2025 pens, extra age classes | Not in the reports or workbooks | Ask USFWS for the facility-by-age records |
| Magnitudes for qualitative mortality events (including E22, E11, E14 and E16) | Most events have no number in the reports or workbooks | Ask USFWS or agree how to assign severity numerically |

# Notes for the model

* `KFNFH_pond_growout` is the stage-specific growth and survival table (mm/day, survival percent, by pond and season, FY2021-2025).
* `KFNFH_mortality_events` and `KFNFH_mortality_pond_monthly` give event frequency/severity and routine mortality.
* `KFNFH_capacity` bounds production; `KFNFH_historical_collection_release` and `KFNFH_hatchery_release` give inputs and outputs by year.
* `age_class` has multi-age values (`"1/2/3"`) where a facility held several age groups in one year. Decide how to allocate mortality and growth in those cases before using it as a stage.
